knowledge.purpose: Semantic heading (h1–h6) that sets visual and outline hierarchy on a surface
useCases: Section title in a marketing layout
Card title in a list of cards
antiPatterns: Pure visual emphasis without semantic outline — use text.text with style overrides
Caption beneath an image — use text.text
knowledge.implementation:
Further use cases:
- Form section header

props.name: gradient
props.type: { enabled: boolean, from: string, via: string, to: string, direction: "to-r" | "to-l" | "to-t" | "to-b" | "to-tr" | "to-tl" | "to-br" | "to-bl" }

jsonSchema.description: Short accent bar to the left of the heading (theme accent token).
Uppercases the text with CSS (beware the Turkish İ/I innerText trap).

props.name: rich
props.description: Opt-in inline emphasis: when true, `text` may carry mini-markdown — **bold**, *italic*, ~~strike~~ (error-token underline), ==mark== (accent highlight with on-accent ink). No HTML is accepted; unknown syntax renders literally.

jsonSchema.description: Move keyboard focus to this heading whenever this value changes after the first render — bind it to what the heading announces, e.g. {{state.step}} on a wizard's step heading, so a keyboard or screen-reader visitor lands on the new step's title. The first render never moves focus. Set, the heading is focusable by script (tabIndex -1), not a Tab stop.

props.name: href
props.description: Puts a link inside the heading: an app path ("/blog/launch"), a URL or "#anchor". The heading text is the link.

props.name: lang
props.description: The language of the heading's text (BCP 47, e.g. "en") when it differs from the page's, written as the element's lang so uppercase follows that language's case rules.
